subject: Aug 30 — elevated streaming response latency (customer briefing)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: ops@crescenthealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Incident notification — elevated streaming response latency

Hi Sam / Crescent ops team,

I’m reaching out with an incident notification: since ~14:40 PDT we’ve observed sustained elevated latency on conversational streaming endpoints that power your live chat flows. Impact we have seen so far:

- Intermittent delayed streaming chunks (200–1200ms extra per chunk) for ~3–5% of sessions.
- A small subset (~0.4%) of long-running conversations experienced repeated chunk retries, resulting in perceived stalls.

What we’re doing now:
- Fallback routing: traffic for your account has been routed to an alternate inference pool with higher spare capacity.
- Edge smoothing: we’ve temporarily increased edge buffer windows to reduce chunk splits.
- Telemetry capture: collected a snapshot of request traces and token cadence (attached).

Suggested actions on your side (short-term):
- If you can, enable polling fallback for sessions experiencing stalls (client-side: set stream=false and poll at 200–500ms) to avoid user-perceived gaps.
- Reduce max_stream_chunk_ms where possible to 100–150ms to limit large chunk reassembly.

We’ll send a technical follow-up in ~60 minutes with more details and a temporary mitigation token you can use for validation. I’ve opened case HS-9421 in our tracker (link below).

Attachments: incident-telemetry-snapshot-20260830.json.gz

—Chloe

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Redwood] Incident notification — elevated streaming response latency

Hi Sam — quick technical update and recommended mitigation steps we applied and you can mirror client-side.

1) Server-side actions (already applied):
- Rerouted your production traffic to an alternate inference pool in the same region with ~40% spare GPU headroom.
- Temporarily increased the stream reconstruction window to smooth chunk boundaries (no code change required on your side).
- Disabled an experimental batching path that was triggering increased tail latency for long contexts (rolled back at 16:00 PDT).

2) Client-side recommendations (immediate):
- If an end-user experiences a stall, switch to polling (set stream=false) and poll every 250ms for up to 6 seconds before attempting to resume streaming.
- Reduce per-chunk target size: max_stream_chunk_ms=120 and set preferred_chunk_tokens=32.
- Implement a soft retry on client with exponential backoff starting at 200ms (max 800ms) for transient chunk failures.

3) Validation token / test route:
- I’ve created a temporary test route token (valid for 2 hours) you can use to validate a few sessions against the alternate pool: TEST-TOKEN-CR-08-30.

4) Next update: we’ll confirm full recovery or share a remediation plan by 17:00 PDT.

Attachments: none (we pulled traces into HS-9421)

—Ben

Subject: INTERNAL — Crescent Health streaming latency escalation

Marissa — internal note. We detected sustained elevated tail latency for streaming that impacted Crescent’s live chat. Ben routed them to alternate pool and rolled back the experimental batching path; we also applied edge smoothing. Sam reported regressions in 95/99 pcts but confirmed they can validate with the test token.

Asking for approval to offer a one-time credit for customer disruption (estimate: 5–8% of August usage). Please advise whether to proceed or if you want finance looped.

I’ll compile a short postmortem once we have root cause and confirm customer is fully recovered.

—Chloe
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Update & post-incident summary — streaming latency

Hi Sam — quick update and summary after our remediation work: your production traffic has been stable on the alternate pool since ~17:10 PDT and telemetry shows 99.9% of sessions have returned to baseline. Thank you for validating with the test token.

Root cause (preliminary): an experimental batching optimization in the realtime runtime produced uneven token cadence for certain long-context requests under sustained load; this increased the occurrence of chunk boundary fragmentation and retries. We rolled that path back at 16:00 PDT which materially reduced tail latency. Engineering has the rollback as the immediate fix; a more robust scheduling patch is in QA.

Customer-facing postmortem (public summary): https://drive.google.com/open?id=postmortem-20260830-public
Internal postmortem (detailed): internal link (shared in HS-9421).

Requested next steps for Crescent:
- Keep the client-side polling fallback available as a safety net for the next 72 hours.
- We will schedule a 30-minute post-incident call tomorrow (Aug 31) to review the long-term mitigations, timing for the scheduler patch, and any billing adjustments.

Attachments: postmortem-20260830-convo-delay.pdf

Please let us know if you’d like the call earlier — we’re standing by.

Thanks again for your patience.

—Chloe
